testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.explanation: Sign the inspection report only if defects were found and then fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Travel faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Think ahead about what you would do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: Mirrors should be used:

options.text: Only when there may be an emergency.
By a helper to monitor your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. Look at both the left and right mirrors.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Fog is very dangerous. Avoid driving in it if possible. If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you need to stop before turning, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind the stop line or crosswalk. Point your front wheels straight ahead. Do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the car in front of you.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull over safely and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over safely and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you get drowsy, stop and sleep. Tired drivers cause many fatal accidents.

questions.question: If you don't know how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure which fire extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials fires, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver exits the vehicle and walks to the back to check position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver exits the vehicle and walks to the back to check position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you leave your seat and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. You can do one look during straight line backing. You can do up to two looks in other exercises.

questions.question: Interstate carriers must display what information on both sides of a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: Federal rules require carriers to display the USDOT number on both sides of every commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Parking brakes:

options.text: Should be tested only after driving some distance.
Should be tested before you drive.
Should be tested on a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be tested before you drive.
questions.explanation: Test the parking brake before you start driving as part of your pre-trip check. If the parking brake does not hold, the vehicle needs to be repaired.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long when shifting gears?

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
The vehicle will be hard to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long when shifting can make it hard to get into the next gear.

questions.question: What should you do if you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under a bridge?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down and find another route if you can.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the driving test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If it is a bus, hold onto the handrail. Getting out incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT need to be in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must show where the trip started and ended, and the Vehicle Identification Number. It does not need to track meals.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are near other drivers, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it is hard to see and other drivers are nearby, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Which of the following can result in being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: You are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
You had a speeding conviction in the last three years.
You missed one question on the hazardous materials test.
You did not pass the hazardous materials test on your first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, have certain felony convictions, have been judged mentally defective, or are seen as a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: What is true about dual tires?

options.text: Both tires do not need to touch the road.
They should not touch each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch each other.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: What comes out when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do if the brake pedal does not build up pressure?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If you lose brake pressure, shift to a lower gear to help slow the vehicle.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, after you drive over a bridge, the examiner may ask you to remember something about it.

options.text: The color of a sign you passed.
How many lanes were on the bridge.
If there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, the examiner may ask you to recall the weight limit posted on a bridge you just drove over.

questions.question: You are driving slowly in a construction zone. You see a construction worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always slow down in construction zones. Slow down even more if you see workers on or near the road.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does an air compressor governor stop pumping air into the tanks?
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What is another name for front end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver from cargo that might move forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces the need for braking. But a retarder can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn it off when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL, what is true about seat belts?

options.text: You do not need to wear one.
You must wear one only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must wear one only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.explanation: For your safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times when operating a commercial motor vehicle (CMV).

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: What is the rule about cell phones while driving a CMV?

options.text: You can hold your phone to receive a call.
You cannot hold your phone to make a call.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot hold your phone to make a call.
questions.explanation: While driving a CMV, you cannot make calls by holding your phone or pressing multiple buttons. You also cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs your ability to drive before you reach the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches a BAC of 0.02 percent after just one drink.

questions.question: Which driver is NOT a hazard?

options.text: A driver who hasn't scraped ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
A driver with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. This includes drivers with ice on windshields, those driving rental trucks without knowing the vehicle's limited rear visibility, and those with cargo blocking windows. Simply driving a pick-up truck does not make someone a hazard.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the air system fills up, test the warning light by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brake system. The warning light should turn on when air pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be on a slope going uphill.
Should be on a slope going downhill.
Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the passenger compartment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil buildup can damage the brakes. You should use manual drains every day.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be:
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers or trailers without sides must be tied down so it does not shift or fall off during transport.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes too much causes them to overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes only when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will be asked to change lanes. Check your surroundings, use your turn signal, and change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:

options.text: Are not required on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: As a truck driver carrying cargo, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your planned route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your planned route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your cargo, watch for overloading or poorly balanced weight, make sure the cargo is properly secured, and ensure it does not block your view or restrict access to emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded and secured it.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers in their vehicle should be seen as:
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not be paying full attention to driving. Be careful when driving near drivers who are distracted.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless it carries hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless it travels through remote areas.
Always have at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always have at least one fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have the right emergency equipment. You should check for at least one fire extinguisher, spare fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for when the vehicle is parked.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by at least one-half when driving on packed snow. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop or turn, so you must drive slower for safety.

questions.question: After a vehicle is started, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.
Should stay on all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right after the engine starts. If a light stays on, the vehicle has a problem.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of the following should not cause concern?

options.text: At least 4/32 of an inch of tread on front tires

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 4/32 of an inch of tread on front tires
questions.explanation: Front tires should have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires should have at least 2/32 of an inch. Do not mix different tire types or sizes. Never use radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use only one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is very important when driving at night.

questions.question: If a driver begins to feel fatigued while driving, they should:

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip quickly.

questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, safely pull off the road and sleep. Drinking coffee or using stimulants is dangerous because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When operating a truck requiring a CDL:

options.text: You are never required to wear a seat belt.
You are required to wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You are required to wear a seat belt only if driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times when operating a commercial vehicle. The driver's seat must always have a seat belt.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction of the turn.
Look in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. If a driver does not signal, their body movement can show that they plan to turn.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Brake harder than with other braking systems.

questions.explanation: Brake normally in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Do not brake any differently than you would in other vehicles.

questions.question: As part of the vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant will be asked to:
questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection test includes checking the oil level. You must show that the oil level is safe for operation.
